status: pilot; freeze after shared-prefix and native sampling acceptance
purpose: Test whether the lower emitted synthesis reasoning observed in the composed Fieldnote workload repeats on CUDA, including a shared-prefix HTTP control.
workload: Full Fieldnote Survey, Standard effort, fresh session/coverage, original Harbor PDF and site map plus Markdown corpus, four reviewed objectives, saved brief and follow-up. Route-explicit question is identical to the completed CUDA memory composed workload.

armMeaning.resident: Pinned Fieldnote orchestration with public Branch sampler settings at stage boundaries; resident trunk/spine and ordinary native abilities.
armMeaning.http: Existing idiomatic LangGraph host behind the same Fieldnote UI, cache_prompt=true, llama-server prefix-cache enabled.
armMeaning.shared-prefix: The same HTTP host and workflow; each system message begins with a stable current brief and source catalog, followed by its complete original stage instructions. Natural request reuse; no synthetic padding or hidden cache priming.

seeds.preflight: 2000 + source index, fixed by pinned coverage API

controls.gpu: one NVIDIA L40S; stacks run sequentially
controls.tracing: Native LLOYAL_DEV=1, instrumented native and server binaries from previous CUDA experiment
controls.outputCap: No explicit synthesis cap on either path; retain context/output-limit failures

order: Random initial arm permutation, cyclic rotation per repetition; one occurrence in each position. Save realized order before any measured run.
acceptance: Fresh preflight and synthesis events present
Four reviewed inquiry objectives retained with original routing
Model/projector/reranker and pinned runtime identities saved
HTTP exact requests, rendered prompts, SSE and cache receipts retained
Shared-prefix synthesis has nonzero server-reported cache_n, with reusable token-prefix evidence
outcomes: Emitted reasoning tokens by stage, post-hoc same GGUF tokenizer
Visible final answer tokens and words
Per-stage generation totals and wall time
Synthesis and workload HTTP prefix-cache reuse
Rubric-scored initial answer and separate follow-up
interpretation: Three repetitions of one synthetic task are exploratory. Full inputs and generated evidence differ. Shared-prefix layout is an input-construction intervention, not a pure cache on/off ablation. Matching sampler settings does not make different execution paths bitwise identical. Reasoning text is not a measure of all internal computation. No causal or quality-equivalence claim from token counts alone.
failurePolicy: Retain every pilot, completed attempt and failure. No unrecorded automatic replacement. Pilot repairs precede a new protocol/source freeze; results with missing acceptance receipts remain ineligible.
